candidate_relations.reason: The reference diagnosis is a composite requiring both recurrent postpartum mastitis AND concurrent lactotroph hyperplasia. C001 correctly identifies the mastitis component with its bacterial etiology (Streptococcus agalactiae), and 'puerperal' aligns with postpartum. However, it entirely omits the lactotroph hyperplasia component, which is supported by the elevated prolactin (72.3 ng/mL), history of cabergoline use, galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and the heterogeneous pituitary MRI findings. The recurrent nature (four episodes) is also not captured. C001 is thus only a partial component of the full composite diagnosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Captures the mastitis component with etiology but omits the concurrent lactotroph hyperplasia component and the recurrent/postpartum characterization

case_quality_flags: Composite diagnosis requires both infectious and endocrine components; candidates addressing only one component will be partial at best
